opening.headline: From demand to a day-ahead price
opening.lede: gridflow-models is a separate Python library that reads gridflow's silver tables. It forecasts GB demand, wind and solar, builds the GB supply stack, and clears demand against that stack for a day-ahead price.
opening.chain_line: Demand less wind and solar is residual demand; the price is where residual demand meets the supply stack.
opening.published_run_line: The published price run uses recorded demand, wind and solar rather than the forecasts, so it gives one price per half-hour.
opening.optional_capability_line: The price model also accepts the three forecasts in place of the recorded values.
opening.scope: It produces forecasts and prices for research. It does not produce orders, positions or P&L.
notes: Headline drops the count on purpose: Bobbo asked for the chain, not five siblings (models-decisions.md).

optional_capability_line describes code that exists (EstimatorInputConfig) but has never run; use it only if the page needs to explain why the forecast models sit above the price. Leave it out if in doubt.

the workbench produces forecasts and stack outputs; it does not produce orders, positions or P&L

models.name: Day-ahead demand
models.job: Forecasts GB national demand for every half-hour of the next day, as a spread of quantiles in MW.
models.method: LightGBM quantile regression, one model per quantile from 0.05 to 0.95, with a conformal widening of the outer band. Version 1 uses calendar terms and demand already published at issue time; version 2 adds weather.

status_code.kind: probabilistic estimator, fitted per walk-forward fold

models.status_line: Both versions pass their gates and are validated. The scores come from stored walk-forward backtests.

models.name: Fundamentals SMP
models.drawing: stack crossed by a demand line (the draft's smp mark)
models.job: Clears residual demand against the stack every half-hour for a GB day-ahead price, scored against Elexon's market index.
models.method: Residual demand is demand less wind and solar, less signed hydro, interconnector, OTHER and pumped storage flows. The price is the marginal cost where that demand meets the stack, floored at −500 GBP/MWh.

status_code.kind: hybrid probabilistic estimator with a no-op fit; published backtest runs in gold

models.status_line: It has nothing to fit. Its published run clears recorded demand, wind and solar, so each half-hour gets one price, not a spread.

reading_scores.heading: Reading the scores
reading_scores.copy: Every score here is a backtest held in gold. Pinball loss at the median is half the mean absolute error of the median forecast, in MW. Coverage is the share of outturns inside the 5 to 95% band. A demand version passes when median pinball is at most 1,500 MW, coverage is within 0.05 of 0.90 and no quantiles cross. Price scores are in GBP/MWh against Elexon's APXMIDP market index.
